work.title: Pointwise representation counts for Eisenstein restricted sums
work.abstract: Let \(A\) consist of the positive integers supported on primes \(1\bmod 3\), including \(1\). We count distinct ordered representations \(n=a+b\) for \(n\equiv2\bmod6\) and \(n=a+3b\) for \(n\equiv4\bmod6\), with \(a,b\in A\). In either family prescribe an interval of length \(H\) centered at \(x\) for one actual summand. Put \(M=\min(x,n-x)\). For every fixed \(0<\varepsilon<1\), if \(H\le M\) and \(H^3\ge n^{1+\varepsilon}M\), the count has order \(HJ(n)/\log n\) for every sufficiently large admissible \(n\). Here \(J(n)\) is the product of \((p-1)/(p-2)\) over the odd primes \(p\equiv2\bmod3\) dividing \(n\). In particular, central windows of width \(n^\theta\) are allowed for \(2/3<\theta<1\), and windows at a prescribed small summand of size comparable to their width are allowed for \(1/2<\theta<1\). The lower bound combines angular Hecke estimates with a sieve that prescribes small split factors in both summands.

Human-understanding declaration: None of this contribution has been checked and understood by any human.
Additional provenance: This research was initiated and directed by Roy van Rijn. ChatGPT/Codex (OpenAI) and other language models were used extensively for mathematical exploration, proof development, literature review, manuscript drafting and independent internal proof checks. Computational verification used Python to check selected exact local identities, prime-power recurrences and finite residue calculations. The manuscript includes a written analytic proof based on quaternionic Hecke operators and sieve methods.
